transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. It's like... even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or if something at work goes really well, I just can't feel it. The good feelings just aren't there.
How long have you been experiencing this lack of pleasure and inability to feel happiness?
It's been going on for a while now. I'd say... well, it really started right after the retrofit accident. That was about a year and seven months ago.
Since the retrofit accident 20 months ago, have you felt this way continuously, or have there been times when your mood improved or you felt more like yourself?

Honestly, it's... it's been pretty continuous. I can't really think of any times where my mood improved or I felt like my old self again. I keep hoping I'll just snap out of it one day, but... no. It's just been this same flat feeling the whole time.
During the retrofit accident, did you hit your head or lose consciousness at any point?
No, I... I didn't hit my head. I was awake the whole time. I didn't black out or lose consciousness at any point, no. I remember it all happening.

Before the retrofit accident 20 months ago, have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where your mood was unusually high, elevated, or expansive—where you felt on top of the world, needed very little sleep, or had racing thoughts?

No, I... I've never experienced anything like that. Before the accident, my mood was just normal, I guess. I never had days where I felt unusually high or didn't need sleep or anything. It was just... regular life.

You mentioned the flat mood has been continuous for about 20 months since the accident. During those 20 months, has there been even a single day or a few days here and there where you felt notably better, or has it truly been the same every single day without any breaks?

No, there really haven't been any breaks. I mean... I haven't had a single day where I woke up and actually felt better or lighter. It's just been this constant, heavy feeling every single day since it happened. There hasn't been any relief from it.

During these 20 months since the accident, have there been any stretches of time—say, a few weeks or more in a row—where your mood lifted or you felt somewhat better, even if it wasn't back to completely normal?

No, like I was just saying... there hasn't been anything like that. Definitely not for a few weeks. It's just been that same flat, heavy feeling the entire time. There really haven't been any stretches where it lifted at all.

You mentioned this flat, heavy feeling has been continuous for 20 months. But let me ask more specifically: in those first few weeks right after the accident, did this depressed mood start immediately, or did it take a little time—maybe a few days or a week or two—before it set in?
It started right away. I mean, pretty much from the moment it happened, that heaviness just... settled in. There wasn't any delay or anything. It was immediate.

During these 20 months since the accident, have there been any individual days—even just one or two days here and there—where you felt your normal mood return, or has every single day without exception felt the same way?
No, I really haven't. Like I said, it's just been exactly the same every single day. I haven't had a single day where I felt like my old self again, not even for a few hours. It's just constant.

I want to make sure I understand the timeline clearly. In those 20 months since the accident, have you had any week or two where things felt even slightly less heavy or flat than usual—not back to normal, but noticeably better than your baseline?

No, honestly, there hasn't been a single week like that. It's just been a steady line... no ups, no periods where the weight lifted, even a little bit. It's just been the same heavy feeling the whole time.

During these 20 months since the accident, have you ever had a period where you felt more energetic or productive than usual, took on more projects or activities, or noticed you needed less sleep than normal?

No, nothing like that. I haven't had any extra energy or taken on new projects. If anything, it's just been the opposite. I definitely haven't felt like I needed less sleep... I'm just tired all the time. So, no, no periods of feeling energetic or productive at all.

On a scale where 0 is the worst you've felt and 10 is your normal self before the accident, what number would you say describes how you feel most days now, and has that number stayed pretty much the same, or has it shifted up or down at all over these 20 months?

I'd say... it's probably around a 2 or a 3 most days. And no, it really hasn't shifted up or down. It's just stayed right there at that same low number for the whole 20 months. Just a constant 2 or 3.

When you think back over these 20 months, have there been any individual days where your mood felt noticeably worse than that 2 or 3 level you described—days where things felt even heavier or more unbearable than usual?

No, not really. I mean, it's just been a steady two or three the whole time. I haven't really noticed any specific days that were worse than the others. It's just a constant, heavy feeling every day, pretty much exactly the same. So, no, no days that stand out as being worse.

I know you've said the mood has been steady, but I want to ask it a different way: if you think back over these 20 months, are there any stretches—even just a few days to a week—where you felt even slightly less depressed or the heaviness eased up just a bit, even if it wasn't much of an improvement?

No, honestly, it hasn't eased up at all. It's just been... flat. Like I said, just that same low point every day. I haven't had any stretches where I felt even a little bit lighter or less down. It's just been a constant weight this whole time.

I want to go back to something. You mentioned your mood has been around a 2 or 3 out of 10 for all 20 months. But thinking back carefully—has there ever been any stretch of 2 weeks or longer where that number went up to, say, a 4 or 5 or higher, before it came back down to that 2 or 3?

No, I don't think so. I know you're trying to see if there was a break in it, but... no. It really hasn't gone up to a 4 or 5 for two weeks, or even a few days. It's just been that same low level, day in and day out. I haven't had any periods where it lifted like that.

I understand you've been feeling this heavy, flat way for all 20 months. But let me ask it very simply: in those 20 months, has there been even a single morning where you woke up and felt completely normal—like the depression just wasn't there that day—before it came back?
No. I mean, I really wish I could say yes, but... no. There hasn't been a single morning where I woke up and felt normal. It's just always there.

I know you've described this as constant, but I want to be very precise: thinking back over the entire 20 months, has there been any single period of 2 weeks or longer where your mood was noticeably better than that 2 or 3 level you mentioned—even if it wasn't back to normal, just meaningfully improved—before returning to that low level?

No, there hasn't been. I... I know you're trying to find some kind of break in it, but I just haven't had one. It hasn't been better for two weeks, or even a few days. It's just stayed right there at that same low point the whole time.

I want to ask about the opposite direction now. In these 20 months since the accident, have you ever had a stretch of several days or more where your mood was noticeably better or more upbeat than your baseline—where you felt more optimistic, more talkative, or more energetic than you normally do, even if it wasn't extreme?

No, definitely not. I haven't had anything like that. I haven't felt upbeat or optimistic at all since the accident, let alone for several days. It's just been... flat and low, like I said. No bursts of energy or anything like that.

This presentation is consistent with Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, severe (F32.9) rather than the chronic but typically milder dysthymia. The acute onset following the accident, complete absence of any symptom relief over 20 months, and severity level (2-3/10) point to F32.9.

opening_question.intent: Establish rapport and identify the chief complaint that brings the patient to the psychiatric clinic
opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, and hopelessness that began immediately following a traumatic accident 20 months ago and has remained continuously severe without remission. While the trauma exposure and temporal relationship to the accident raise consideration of Persistent Depressive Disorder with Traumatic Origin (F34.1) and Prolonged Grief Disorder/Adjustment Disorder (F43.12), the severity, pervasiveness, and complete absence of any mood fluctuation or partial remission over 20 months, combined with explicit denial of manic/hypomanic episodes, most clearly fits Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Severe Without Psychotic Features (F32.9). The continuous nature without any breaks, even brief ones, and the profound functional impact indicate a single major depressive episode of extended duration rather than a persistent dysthymic condition.

confirmed_symptoms: Persistent depressed mood described as 'flat, heavy feeling' since accident
Continuous depressed mood for entire 20-month period with no remission
Mood rating of 2-3 out of 10 maintained consistently throughout duration
No single day of normal mood return or relief
Complete inability to feel pleasure or happiness
Cannot enjoy previously pleasurable activities (Sunday routines with wife)
Cannot feel satisfaction from positive work events
Described as 'good feelings just aren't there'
Persistent fatigue and tiredness throughout 20-month period
No periods of decreased need for sleep
Absence of increased energy or productivity
Hopelessness about recovery ('keep hoping I'll just snap out of it one day, but... no')
Pervasive sense of heaviness and burden

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms present continuously for 20 months (approximately 1 year 7 months) since the retrofit accident, with onset immediate and no remission periods whatsoever
additional_requirements: No history of manic or hypomanic episodes confirmed
No head injury or loss of consciousness during accident
Complete absence of mood fluctuation, daily variation, or any remission periods
Severe depressive symptoms with continuous 2-3/10 mood rating
